text:
alex: hitting a weird bundler/runtime mismatch when we import the JS SDK into an edge-target app. build works in node target but fails in vite+edge with `ReferenceError: require is not defined` and in webpack it becomes `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'default')`

alex: minimal case: TS app (vite, target=webworker), import like `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference-js'` -> runtime blows up.

alex: package.json of the SDK looks like this:
```json
{
  "name": "redwood-inference-js",
  "main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
  "module": "dist/index.esm.js",
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js",
      "import": "./dist/index.esm.js"
    }
  }
}
```

alex: repro steps I used:
1) npx create-vite@latest repro --template vanilla-ts
2) set `target: 'webworker'` in vite config
3) `npm i ../local/redwood-inference-js` (local packed tar)
4) import default as above and run `vite preview` -> runtime error on page load

priya: do you have a browser/edge bundle build log? is vite doing prebundling?

alex: yes, vite prebundle shows it transforming the cjs file sometimes, but when SSR/edge mode kicks in it resolves the `exports` conditional to the cjs path which relies on CommonJS stuff ("require"). that kills it in ESM-only runtimes.

mike: this is classic exports-conditional resolution mismatch with bundlers. Vite sometimes resolves to the `require` side during optimizeDeps or the dev server. Have you tried `ssr: { noExternal: ['redwood-inference-js'] }` or adding `optimizeDeps.include`? that forces ESM resolution.

alex: tried `noExternal`, helped for dev server but prod bundle still ends up referencing `dist/index.cjs.js` in the worker runtime. Rollup/webpack treat `exports` differently.

jess: thanks for the write-up — sounds like our published package is exposing a CJS path that some bundlers pick for edge builds. can you paste the exact runtime stack? also curious whether `import * as Redwood from 'redwood-inference-js'` vs default import changes things.

alex: stack trace (chromium edge worker): `ReferenceError: require is not defined at dist/index.cjs.js:12:5`

alex: tried `import * as Redwood` -> `Redwood.default` is undefined in webpack build, so consumers get either `undefined` or runtime require error depending on bundler.

mike: quick repro suggestion for us to debug: a tiny sandbox with vite+target webworker + a single import. if we can reproduce we can test different `exports` shapes.

alex: i pushed a minimal repro: https://github.com/alex/repro-redwood-bundle (private link) — steps in README.

jess: ok I'll open an issue in the SDK repo. likely fixes: (a) ensure `exports.import` is prioritized in publish (b) ship an ESM-only entry for browser/edge under `browser` field or `exports."./browser"` or (c) add an npm dist-tag with ESM artifacts. we should also add a note in DX guide about `ssr.noExternal` for vite.

jess: also can we add a CI check that bundles the package with rollup/vite/webpack cloud workers targets? would catch this earlier.

mike: for bundler-specific immediate workarounds:
- Vite: `optimizeDeps.include = ['redwood-inference-js']` and `ssr.noExternal` for SSR/preview builds
- Rollup (used by some build systems): add `@rollup/plugin-commonjs` before any other transforms or prefer `resolve.mainFields = ['module','main']`
- Webpack: set `resolve.mainFields = ['browser','module','main']` and `type: 'javascript/esm'` on modules if you can control loader

alex: workaround that worked for me for now: publish a tiny shim `dist/edge.js` that re-exports the esm build and set `exports."./edge"` to point to it. then import from `redwood-inference-js/edge` in the app. ugly but unblocks us.

build-bot: CI failure in sdk/nightly: bundle-edge-test failed on node 18 with error `require is not defined` (see logs) :warning:

jess: thanks, added to sprint. i'll ping when we have a patch. for now i'll add a short note in devex docs summarizing the bundler tips and the temporary `redwood-inference-js/edge` shim pattern.

priya: nice writeup alex. can you also add the exact `vite.config.ts` and `tsconfig.json` from the repro to the issue so we can reproduce locally?

alex: will do, pushed config to the repro repo now. cheers :rocket:
